english.title: Aid / abet driving of a mechanically propelled vehicle without due care and attention
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) aided, abetted, counselled or procured **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to drive a mechanically propelled vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a

(A)_[ road,]_
(B)_[ public place,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD/PLACE AND LOCATION..), without due care and attention
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3 of the Road Traffic Act 1988, section 44 of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) See section 13A of the Road Traffic Act 1988 for the disapplication of section 3 in relation to authorised motoring events.
(ii) Statement of Facts procedure applies - see end of document for wording.
(iii) The level of fine was raised to level five by section 23 of the Road Safety Act 2006.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.Obligatory endorsement - licence endorsed three to nine penalty points.Discretionary disqualification.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
